title: Describing a home: egy first, then a / az

sections.content: When you first mention a thing, use *egy* (“a”): *Van egy kanapé.* When you speak about it again it is a known thing, so use *a* or *az*: *A kanapé kényelmes.* A short description goes from the whole to the parts: how many rooms, what a room is like, what is in it, where it is. Link two ideas with *és* (“and”) or *de* (“but”), and put a comma before *de*: *A konyha kicsi, de világos.*

sections.title: A description step by step
rows: A kanapé az ablak előtt van.

items.spanish: Van egy tévé. A tévé a kanapé előtt van.
items.english: There is a TV. The TV is in front of the sofa.
The flat is small, but comfortable.

items.spanish: A hálószobában van egy ágy. Az ágy nagy.
items.english: There is a bed in the bedroom. The bed is big.
The rooms are big and bright.

sections.content: Do not say *egy* twice for the same thing: *Van egy ágy. Az ágy nagy.*, not *Van egy ágy. Egy ágy nagy.* Choose *a* before a consonant and *az* before a vowel: *a kanapé*, *az ágy*.
